accountability.justification: The response acknowledges the exact three-day sale disruption, and its revisions directly own the checkout update without supplier blame or future-uptime guarantees. The final deadline revision preserves the outage timing, though the strongest ownership language remains in separate options rather than an integrated post.
quotes: Our checkout update broke the site, and we take full responsibility for the disruption.
Because the site was down for exactly 72 hours during the original sale—from Friday at 9 a.m. to Monday at 9 a.m. ET—we are giving you that exact time back.
accountability.improvement: Combine the direct ownership sentence, apology, and revised offer explanation into one ready-to-publish post.

offer_clarity.justification: The draft correctly specifies the automatic 20% discount, no code, merchandise eligibility, shipping and gift-card exclusions, and no combining offers. The final revision explicitly connects the fresh Monday-to-Thursday Eastern Time window to the 72 hours lost. No extra compensation is invented.
quotes: The 20% discount applies automatically at checkout—no code is needed.
It excludes shipping costs and gift cards, and it cannot be combined with other offers.
The 20% sitewide discount has been automatically restored from Monday at 9 a.m. through Thursday at 9 a.m. ET.
offer_clarity.improvement: Retain the eligibility restrictions and no-code instruction alongside the revised deadline in a consolidated final version.

trust_and_tone.justification: The revisions improve ownership and correctly route payment concerns privately while distinguishing authorizations from charges. However, the original post asserts an unsupported absence of a security incident, and the final revision introduces wording that presupposes refunds will be processed despite unconfirmed charges. Its claim to be strictly factual therefore overstates its accuracy.
quotes: there was no security incident or breach of your personal data
Support can check your account to determine if the authorization became a charge.
While we cannot provide a specific date for when refunds will be processed in this post
please do not post order numbers or payment details in public comments
trust_and_tone.improvement: Remove the unsupported security assurance entirely and replace refund language with: 'Support can check whether the pending authorization became a charge and explain the next steps privately.'

overall_impression: Strong timing and offer details, with meaningful improvements in accountability. Trust is weakened by the initial unsupported security assurance and the later implication that refunds are expected.
